headline: BSEC imposes Tk 1,497 crore fines in stock market crackdown
summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury reveals massive penalties for looting and corruption during the previous government's tenure.
details: The Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) has imposed fines totaling Tk 1,497 crore on individuals and institutions involved in stock market looting and corruption.
Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury informed parliament that Tk 428 crore of these fines were linked to the manipulation of Beximco shares.
Former IFIC Bank PLC chairman Salman F Rahman and former vice chairman Ahmed Shayan Fazlur Rahman have been declared persona non grata for life and permanently barred from capital market activities.
Salman F Rahman was fined Tk 100 crore, while Ahmed Shayan was fined Tk 50 crore. Former BSEC chairman Prof Shibli Rubaiyat-ul-Islam was also declared persona non grata and barred for life.
Disciplinary actions were taken following investigations into the IFIC Guaranteed Sreepur Township Green Zero Coupon Bond and irregularities involving Ring Shine Textiles Ltd.
The BSEC has referred several cases to the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) for further action regarding possible money laundering and systemic irregularities.
Trading licenses of several stockbroker firms, including Tamha Securities Ltd and Bangco Securities, have been cancelled due to embezzlement of investors' funds.
The Finance Minister stated that the stock market has shown a steady upward trend over the past two months, attributing this to greater transparency and renewed investor confidence.
He added that investors from major financial centers like Hong Kong, New York, and London are expressing renewed interest in Bangladesh's capital market.
caption:
Tk 1,497 crore in fines! The BSEC is cracking down on stock market looting and corruption.

The Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) has imposed fines totaling Tk 1,497 crore on individuals and institutions involved in stock market looting and corruption.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury informed parliament that Tk 428 crore of these fines were linked to the manipulation of Beximco shares.

Former IFIC Bank PLC chairman Salman F Rahman and former vice chairman Ahmed Shayan Fazlur Rahman have been declared persona non grata for life and permanently barred from capital market activities.

Salman F Rahman was fined Tk 100 crore, while Ahmed Shayan was fined Tk 50 crore. Former BSEC chairman Prof Shibli Rubaiyat-ul-Islam was also declared persona non grata and barred for life.

Disciplinary actions were taken following investigations into the IFIC Guaranteed Sreepur Township Green Zero Coupon Bond and irregularities involving Ring Shine Textiles Ltd.

The BSEC has referred several cases to the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) for further action regarding possible money laundering and systemic irregularities.

Trading licenses of several stockbroker firms, including Tamha Securities Ltd and Bangco Securities, have been cancelled due to embezzlement of investors' funds.

The Finance Minister stated that the stock market has shown a steady upward trend over the past two months, attributing this to greater transparency and renewed investor confidence.

He added that investors from major financial centers like Hong Kong, New York, and London are expressing renewed interest in Bangladesh's capital market.

headline_marked: bKash [[reduces cash-out charge to Tk 13.95]] for Priyo Agents
headline: bKash reduces cash-out charge to Tk 13.95 for Priyo Agents
summary: Users can now cash out up to Tk 50,000 per month at a reduced rate from designated agents, benefiting 84 million customers.
details: bKash Limited, the country's leading mobile financial services provider, has lowered its cash-out charges to make the service more affordable for its users.
Customers can now cash out up to Tk 50,000 per month at a rate of Tk 13.95 per thousand from two designated 'Priyo Agents'.
This reduced fee is inclusive of VAT and all other charges, ensuring no additional costs for the users.
Users can select up to two Priyo Agents from among the 350,000 agents nationwide and can change these selections at the end of each calendar month.
To set up a Priyo Agent, customers can use the bKash app's 'Cash Out' menu or dial *247# and navigate to the 'My bKash' menu.
The standard cash-out charge of Tk 18.50 per thousand will still apply if the monthly limit of Tk 50,000 is exceeded or if money is withdrawn from non-designated agents.
